text: Finance and Ops have both been running their reports for a good while now, built right on top of the nightly refresh from Lesson 8 — EventBridge triggering the Glue ETL job, which on success triggers a small job that re-runs the COPY into fact orders. It's been working reliably, night after night. Then, one morning, it stops.

Someone on the Finance team emails: this morning's revenue numbers look stale, they match yesterday's totals exactly. Or maybe you just notice it yourself — the scheduled load job's run shows a failure overnight. Either way, the signal is the same. That's a real incident, and stale numbers aren't something to act on by guessing. The first job is the same discipline this course has used for every bug so far: reproduce the problem yourself, under known conditions, before touching anything.

So open the Redshift Query Editor and run the exact COPY statement from Lesson 5, by hand — the very same one the scheduled job runs automatically every single night. Running the real statement manually, instead of just reading the Glue job's log, matters, because it rules out anything specific to the scheduled trigger itself, and isolates the question down to the COPY operation alone.

The statement fails: load into table fact orders failed, check sys load error detail system table for details. That's it — a generic failure, pointing you at a system table, not a specific root cause. It confirms the incident is real and reproducible on demand, which is exactly what you needed before doing anything else. It does not yet tell you whether this is permissions, a malformed file, or a schema mismatch.

Resist the urge to guess which one it probably is. Guessing and checking one thing at a time, without a system to actually confirm the cause, risks fixing something that was never broken while the real problem stays exactly where it was. Right now you have one thing confirmed: the COPY fails, reliably, on demand. Next lesson follows the system table to the actual, confirmed cause.
